transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, I've been feeling light-headed and dizzy when I stand up — getting out of a chair or out of bed. It's been happening for a while now and it's a bit worrying.
Can you tell me how much this has been affecting your day-to-day life, and whether you have any allergies or have had bad reactions to medicines?
I've stopped going to my Tuesday lunch club because I'm worried about feeling faint on the bus. And no, I've no allergies to medicines that I know of, and I've not had any bad reactions before.

Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have started or changed recently — including what they’re for and how often you take them — and any long-term health problems, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays you’ve had?

I take a water tablet, bendroflumethiazide, every morning and I've been on that for years, plus paracetamol up to three times a day for my hip pain. About two and a half weeks ago the practice nurse added a new blood-pressure tablet, amlodipine 5 mg once a day, and I also take a small tablet for my stomach each morning but I can't remember its name. I've had high blood pressure for about 15 years and osteoarthritis in both hips — I've not had any operations or hospital stays.
How much does the light-headed feeling when you stand up affect what you’re able to do day to day?
It mainly stops me getting about — I've given up my Tuesday lunch club because I'm worried about feeling faint on the bus. Otherwise I just take things slowly when I get up.
When you get that light-headed or dizzy feeling on standing, is there anything else you notice at the same time?
No, nothing else — no chest pain, no palpitations, no blackouts, and no weakness in my arms or legs. It's just the swimmy, about-to-faint feeling when I stand up.
When you get that swimmy, about-to-faint feeling on standing, where in your body do you feel it most — and does it move or spread anywhere?
It's mostly in my head — a light, swimmy feeling — and it doesn't spread anywhere else as far as I've noticed.

Besides the medicines you’ve told me about — the water tablet, paracetamol, amlodipine, and the small stomach tablet — are you taking anything else, such as medicines for your blood pressure or hips at other times of day, any inhalers, eye drops, creams, injections or patches, or anything you buy without a prescription like painkillers, vitamins or herbal remedies?
No, that's everything — I don't take anything else, no inhalers, drops, creams or anything from the chemist like vitamins or herbal remedies.

How much does that swimmy feeling when you stand up affect your day — would you say it's mild and easy to ignore, moderate and a bit of a nuisance, or severe and it really gets in the way, or you're not sure?
I'd say it's moderate to severe — I'd rate it about 6 out of 10. It's more than a nuisance; I nearly fell once and had to grab the kitchen worktop.

Could you describe how these swimmy spells tend to come and go — for example, whether they’re there all the time or happen in episodes, how often they come on, how long each one lasts, and whether there’s a time of day they’re more likely?

They come in episodes rather than being there all the time — several times a day. Each one lasts less than a minute and settles if I sit back down for a minute. They're worst first thing in the morning and when I stand up quickly.

To make sure I have the full picture, is there anything else you see a doctor or nurse about regularly, or any other health conditions your medicines are for — like what the water tablet and the small stomach tablet are for — or any operations or hospital stays you haven’t mentioned? It’s completely fine if there’s nothing else.
The water tablet is for my blood pressure, and the small white one is for my stomach, though I can't remember its name. As for operations or hospital stays, no, I've not had any.
Can you tell me when you first noticed this light-headed, dizzy feeling when standing up, and whether it came on suddenly or gradually — and if anything seemed to set it off at that time?
Oh, it's been going on for months, I think.
Is there anything else about your medicines you’d like to add — anything else you take regularly or now and then that we haven’t talked about?
No, there's nothing else — that's all the medicines I take.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
